periods.activity_title: A Busy Street: Picture Walk and Observation

tasks_in_class.task_brief: Picture reading (pp.102–103): observe the busy street and answer questions on shops, animals, dustbins, and the man with a white cane.

time_bands.activity: Teacher conducts a picture walk across the full street scene on pages 102–103, pointing out each area — shops, road, sky — and inviting students to say what they notice. No questions yet; the aim is unhurried looking.

Picture reading ("observe shops, vehicles, animals, and people"): teacher poses questions one at a time — what stands on both sides of the street, what the two differently coloured dustbins tell us, why the man in dark glasses carries a white cane, and which animals can be spotted. Students respond by pointing and speaking in short phrases or sentences.

Picture reading ("count and name"): teacher asks how many bullock carts are visible and invites students to name every animal they can find. Students share answers aloud; teacher reinforces correct observations with a brief confirmation.

Teacher draws attention to the kite, rainbow, and birds in the sky above the street, asking students what they see there. The unit closes with each student saying one thing they found most surprising or interesting in the picture.

periods.teacher_notes: The street scene packs many details across two pages; students often fix on a single corner and miss the sky, the rooftop cat, or the waste-segregation dustbins — guide eyes systematically from ground to sky. The two-colour dustbin detail (blue and green for waste segregation) is an environmental-awareness point worth a brief explanation if students are unfamiliar. Students who cannot immediately name the ice gola can describe the colour or shape — accept descriptive answers and supply the name.

periods.activity_title: Talking About the Street: Guided Conversation and Sharing

tasks_in_class.task_brief: Picture reading (pp.102–103): oral discussion of the busy street scene — observation and personal experience sharing.

time_bands.activity: Teacher reopens the textbook to pages 102–103, giving students a quiet moment to look at the busy street scene again. Teacher then asks: "What is the first thing your eye goes to in this picture?" Students share one-word or one-phrase answers around the class.

Picture reading ("talk about what is happening in the street"): teacher guides a conversation — what each shop sells, what the bullock cart might be carrying, where the children with ice golas might be going. Students are encouraged to speak in full sentences, and partners briefly exchange their ideas before sharing with the class.

Teacher shifts the conversation to personal experience: "Have you seen a market street like this one? What did you notice? Was there a fruit stall, animals, or something colourful?" Students take turns describing their own neighbourhood or market, connecting the picture to lived experience.

Each student shares one sentence: something they see in the picture that they have also seen in real life, or something in the picture they have never seen before. Teacher closes by naming two or three community details from the street — the woman walking her dog, the man with the cane, the waste bins — and affirming that everyday streets carry many interesting stories.

periods.teacher_notes: Having looked carefully at the street scene — shops, animals, people, and sky — students now use it as a springboard for their own words and memories. Some students may find it easier to speak in their home language first; accept this and gently guide them toward an English sentence. If the class is lively, a quick pair-share before whole-class sharing keeps every voice active rather than just the confident speakers.

items.item_stem: Look at the picture of the busy street on Textbook pages 102–103. Which of the following can you see on BOTH sides of the street?

options.label: B
options.text: A bullock cart loaded with sacks

what_each_option_reveals.B: The student may have noticed the bullock cart prominently but confused a single road-centre object with something on both sides.
what_each_option_reveals.C: The student focused on the children's activity, which appears in one part of the scene rather than along both sides.
what_each_option_reveals.D: The student picked out a memorable single figure on the road rather than identifying what lines both sides of the street.

items.item_stem: Look at the picture of the busy street on Textbook pages 102–103. There are two dustbins near the food stall — one blue and one green. Why do you think the dustbins are two different colours? Write one or two sentences.

teacher_guide.suggested_answer: The two dustbins are different colours so that people can put different kinds of rubbish in each one — this is called waste segregation. Blue and green bins help keep the area clean by separating different types of waste.

items.item_stem: Look at the picture of the busy street on Textbook pages 102–103. Which one person or animal in the picture do you find most interesting? Choose one and say TRUE or FALSE for each statement below.

options.text: A woman in a green sari walks with a small dog on a leash in the picture.
The man in dark glasses is riding a bicycle.
A herd of goats is crossing the street.
The cat is sitting near the two dustbins.

teacher_guide.suggested_answer: 1 — True: the picture shows a woman in a green sari walking a small dog. 2 — False: the man in dark glasses is walking and holding a white cane, not riding a bicycle. 3 — True: a herd of goats is shown crossing the street. 4 — False: the cat sits on a rooftop near a 'Study Point' board, not near the dustbins.

items.item_stem: Look at the busy street on Textbook pages 102–103. Imagine you are standing on that street. Tell your teacher or partner: what do you see, what do you hear, and does it remind you of any street or market you have visited? Speak for a short time in English.

expected_elements: Names at least two things seen in the street.
Describes a sound or activity happening there.
Links the picture to a personal memory or place.
